chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam from Abdullah ibn Kathir al-Arjani, who said:

I accompanied Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on the road to Mecca from Medina, and he stayed in a place called Usfan. Then we passed by a black mountain on the left side of the road, solitary and desolate. I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, how desolate this mountain is! I have not seen a mountain like it on the road.'

He said, 'O Ibn Kathir, do you know what this mountain is? This is the mountain called Al-Kamad, and it is over a valley from the valleys of Hell, where the killers of Husayn (peace be upon him) are entrusted by Allah.'

The waters of Hell flow beneath it, from Al-Ghisleen, Al-Sadeed, and Al-Hameem, and what emerges from its mud is Khabal, and what emerges from Al-Hawiya. And whenever I passed by this mountain on my journey, I would stop, and I would see them crying out for help and supplicating humbly.

And indeed, I look at the killers of my father, and I say to them: 'This is what they did. When they gained power, they did not show us mercy. They killed us, deprived us of our rights, and attacked our due, and monopolized the authority for themselves while excluding us. So may Allah not show mercy to one who shows mercy to you. Taste the consequence of what you did, for Allah is not unjust to the servants.'

key_terms.الصَّدِید: Al-Sadeed, a river or water of Hell
key_terms.الْحَمِیم: Al-Hameem, a river or water of Hell
key_terms.الْغِسْلِین: Al-Ghisleen, a river or water of Hell
key_terms.الْهَاوِیَهِ: Al-Hawiya, a deep pit or abyss in Hell
key_terms.جَبَلُ الْکَمَد: Mountain of Sorrow/Grief, a specific mountain in Hell
key_terms.خَبَال: Khabal, a type of pus or filth from Hell

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Jabal al-Kamad in Shia tradition regarding the killers of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the cosmological significance of Jabal al-Kamad as a physical manifestation of Hell’s valleys, specifically designated for the killers of Imam Husayn (a.s.). Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) personifies the martyrs’ ongoing supplication, using their eternal cries to remind the oppressors of their missed opportunity for mercy when they held power, thereby illustrating the Shia concept of *Haqq al-Husayn* extending into the afterlife. The passage underscores divine justice (*‘Adl*) by linking the physical geography of the earth to the spiritual reality of Hell, where the killers’ own deeds become their torment.
